chunks: When the hypocrites come to you, they say: 'We affirm that you are the Apostle of God.' God indeed knows you are His Apostle. God bears witness that the hypocrites are indeed liars.

key_terms.إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُ اللَّهِ: Indeed you are the Apostle of God
key_terms.الْمُنَافِقُونَ: The hypocrites, those who outwardly profess faith but inwardly conceal disbelief

ai.seo_question: What do the hypocrites say to the Prophet and what does God witness about them?
ai.summary: This verse, the opening of Surah Al-Munafiqun, captures the formal yet hollow declaration of the hypocrites who used the phrase 'Ashhadu annaka rasul Allah' to mask their inner kufr. Shia exegesis, such as in Al-Mizan, emphasizes that while their tongues affirmed the Prophet's status, their hearts rejected it, making their testimony invalid in the sight of God. The verse establishes the distinction between outward profession (zahir) and inward belief (batin), a key theme in understanding the spiritual state of the early Muslim community.
